passage:
A city map showed parks, museums, and bus stops, but not public toilets. A student with a medical condition said this made travel difficult.
Her class created a map of public toilets with opening hours, cleanliness notes, and accessibility information.
Many residents found it useful: parents with children, older people, delivery workers, and tourists.
The project showed that dignity often depends on basic facilities.
Urban planning is not only about impressive buildings. It is also about ordinary human needs. A city that ignores toilets may look modern while making daily life harder for many people.
